quote: Vermont's \$1,303 per-discharge administrative cost gap versus the national benchmark
correct_fact: AHS Nov 2025: management and administrative (labor) cost per adjusted discharge, PPS: VT $2,730 vs benchmark $1,427, difference $1,303 (2023 NASHP via CMS). Benchmark = US 75th percentile non-profit hospital, weighted by adjusted discharges. CAHs report no such data.
source_url: AHS Health Care System Transformation Report, Nov 1, 2025 (local copy: book-audit/deep/sources/ahs_act68_report_2025-11.txt)
source_quote: Management and Administrative Cost per Adjusted Discharge      PPS: $2,730 ... PPS: $1,427 ... PPS: $1,303
notes: The gap is a PPS-only weighted average. Per-hospital (Appendix C): UVMMC $3,826, Rutland $2,432, SVMC $1,676, CVMC $1,651, NMC $1,599, BMH $1,462. So UVMMC drives nearly all of it. See finding on the $100M claim.

quote: 14-hospital system
correct_fact: Vermont has 14 general acute hospitals (6 PPS, 8 CAH).
source_quote: 14 general hospitals listed for VT besides Vermont Psychiatric Care Hospital and Brattleboro Retreat (FY2023 cost reports)

quote: AHS has statutory deadlines --- hospital transformation plans by early 2026, RBP by FY2027, global budgets by FY2028, the Statewide Strategic Plan by January 2028.
correct_fact: Only the Strategic Plan date (Jan 15, 2028) is an AHS statutory deadline. The 'early 2026' transformation-plan date was set administratively by AHS (draft plans due Jan 15, final plans Mar 15, 2026), not by statute. RBP and global budgets are GMCB duties: RBP to begin 'not later than hospital fiscal year 2027' (GMCB: methodology by rule in 2027, maximum rates effective HFY2028); global budgets 'beginning not later than HFY2028, to the extent that resources are available' for one or more non-critical-access hospitals, and all hospitals by HFY2030.
source_quote: Beginning not later than hospital fiscal year 2028, to the extent that resources are available, the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals. (Act 68) / Draft plans are due to AHS on January 15 / Final plans are due March 15 (AHS, Jan 14, 2026)
proposed_new_text: The transformation runs on hard dates --- hospital transformation plans set by AHS for early 2026, reference-based pricing that GMCB must begin by hospital fiscal year 2027, the first global budgets for non-critical-access hospitals by FY2028 (to the extent resources are available), and AHS's Statewide Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan due January 15, 2028.
notes: See VERIFIED_FACTS Act 68 section.

quote: It has a constrained budget (\$4.2M in appropriated state funds, plus \$195M in RHT Program capital).
correct_fact: $4.2M is confirmed: Act 68 Sec. 18 gave AHS $2.2M General Fund plus $2M Health IT-Fund. The error is calling the $195M 'capital'. It is Vermont's FFY2026 RHT award ($195,053,740), one year of a five-year program, and it funds programs, not capital; AHS's own report counts $6.95M in total state transformation funds once the $2.75M BAA money is included.

quote: Rather than closing unexpectedly and leaving communities without any healthcare access, Oliver Wyman's blueprint proposes orderly conversion to one of three alternative models: Rural Emergency Hospital (REH --- 24/7 emergency and observation without inpatient beds), Community Ambulatory Care Center (CACC --- outpatient and primary care services), or a Care at Home support hub.
correct_fact: OW's three restructuring options: REH = 'Maintain emergency department and minimal IP beds to manage transfers to regional centers' (24-hr ED; 'IP 2 beds + SNF'). CACC = 'Grow ambulatory services and offer extended urgent care hours' (16-hr urgent care; SNF + rehab + mental health beds; ambulatory surgery). Care at Home Support = 'Support partner hospital's care-at-home program through referrals and back-end services'. The CACC is not a primary-care centre. Federal REH rules bar acute inpatient beds (a distinct-part SNF is allowed), which conflicts with OW's '2 beds'.
source_quote: Rural Emergency Hospital (REH) Community Ambulatory Care Center (CACC) Care at Home Support / Maintain emergency department and minimal IP beds to manage transfers to regional centers / Grow ambulatory services and offer extended urgent care hours to manage hospital transfers / Support partner hospital's care-at-home program through referrals and back-end services
proposed_new_text: Rather than closing unexpectedly and leaving communities without any healthcare access, Oliver Wyman's report lays out three restructuring options: a Rural Emergency Hospital (REH --- a 24-hour emergency department that transfers patients needing admission to regional centers), a Community Ambulatory Care Center (CACC --- expanded ambulatory services and extended-hours urgent care, potentially with skilled-nursing, rehabilitation, or mental-health beds), or a Care at Home support role for a partner hospital's home-based program.

proposed_new_text: The honest answer, reflected in Oliver Wyman's findings and AHS's own public reports, is: not yet --- and AHS's own 2026 structural review chose better coordination over restructuring.
notes: The same 'restructuring' premise appears at md 5308 ('Vermont's AHS restructuring --- creating the Division of Planning and Effectiveness, the HSA Coordinator network ...').

quote: Oliver Wyman identified four specific organizational gaps in AHS that impede transformation execution.
correct_fact: OW's AHS recommendations: align AHS agencies with HSAs and meet regularly with hospitals; fully computerize and integrate AHS subunits; review AHS structure and program list for overlaps; reconfigure sub-units to coordinate health and social services; PMO and facilitation support. The 'Division of Planning and Effectiveness' is a GMCB recommendation. OW did not present 'four gaps'.
source_quote: Align Agency of Human Services agencies with Health Service Areas and meet regularly with hospitals and providers – Fully computerize and integrate Agency of Human Services subunits ... Review existing AHS agency structure and program list to identify overlaps ... Support Needed: Project Management Office and Facilitation Support
proposed_new_text: Oliver Wyman's recommendations point to four organizational gaps that impede transformation execution.

quote: Absence of a Planning and Effectiveness function. AHS currently lacks a dedicated analytical unit that can calculate the financial and access impacts of service site changes, monitor access and affordability across community providers, and track the quality, access, and equity metrics that the Statewide Strategic Plan will require.
correct_fact: These are the functions OW assigned to a new GMCB Division of Planning and Effectiveness ('assist AHS in calculations'), not to an AHS unit.
source_quote: Add Division of Planning and Effectiveness – Calculate impacts of changes in the sites of care on hospital budgets, prices to consumers and availability of long-term care – Monitor access to and affordability of community providers – Monitor progress of transformation / assist AHS in calculations – Monitor progress on Quality / Access/ Equity measures
proposed_new_text: Absence of a Planning and Effectiveness function. Oliver Wyman recommended that the GMCB add a Division of Planning and Effectiveness to calculate the financial and access impacts of service site changes, monitor access and affordability across community providers, and track quality, access, and equity metrics --- assisting AHS with those calculations.
notes: VERIFIED_FACTS.

quote: The Health Care Reform Office, recently reorganized and supplemented by contractor support, is managing a workload that probably requires 50-70% more staff than currently exist.
correct_fact: No source for '50-70% more staff' or a reorganization. AHS's Office of Health Care Reform uses contractors (Manatt, Dr. Craig Jones, analytics vendor under negotiation) and has posted limited-service care transformation positions.
source_quote: contracted transformation support from Manatt, Phelps and Phillips LLP and Dr. Craig Jones
proposed_new_text: The Office of Health Care Reform, supplemented by contractor support, is carrying that workload with a small staff.
notes: Also, 'Act 68 requires AHS to ... oversee RHT Program implementation': RHT is federal (H.R. 1), not an Act 68 duty.
